body.statement: Does there exist a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) with \(p=2\), rational vertices of \(H\), rational entries of \(\Sigma\), rational endpoint intercepts and normals, and a finite prior \(\pi\in\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) having rational support points, rational masses, and unequal total masses on the two endpoint signs, such that the finite curved-score certificate holds for \(\delta_{\pi}\); or are these requirements impossible in two dimensions? An affirmative certificate must instantiate \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\): give a rational \(q\), finite rational box partitions, outward-rounded interval enclosures, and analytic Gaussian-tail bounds proving \(R(\delta_{\pi})\le q\le b(\pi)\). It must also enclose \(B_{\pi}\), its first two derivatives, and \(\mathcal K_{\pi}\) on a rational box meeting a nondegenerate arc \(\Gamma\subset\mathcal Z_{\pi}\), with strictly positive rational lower bounds on the score-gradient norm and on \( |\mathcal K_{\pi}|\), and certify \(B_{\pi}\not\equiv0\). The conclusion \(R(\delta_{\pi})=b(\pi)=v=q\), uniqueness almost everywhere, and \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\) must then follow through \(\mathrm{thm:curved-score-no-index-certificate}\), rather than being assumed.
body.justification: This is the early kill test for the no-one-index branch and demands finite rational data, exact primal-dual closure, and a reproducible interval-arithmetic curvature certificate rather than a numerical plot.
body.gap: Tetenov2012Asymmetric retains threshold structure in point-identified asymmetric problems, and the known partial-identification examples do not certify an unbalanced globally minimax non-halfspace rule.
body.consumer: A certified example would establish that multivariate reporting is sometimes intrinsically necessary; an impossibility theorem would sharply simplify the classification program.
